input:
We're running an asymmetric workload across Cortex-X925 and Cortex-A520 cores in an ARM CSS v2 big.LITTLE configuration. A multithreaded SVE2 application crashes with SIGILL when threads migrate from X925 (SVE2 vector length 512-bit) to A520 (SVE2 vector length 256-bit). The kernel SVE/SIMD context switch log shows:

  [   58.102347] sve: CPU4 SVE VL=512 bits
  [   58.102361] sve: CPU0 SVE VL=256 bits
  [   58.204812] kernel: unhandled level 0 translation fault (11) at 0x00007fff8a200010, esr=0x9600004f

The task is not pinned to a CPU set and prctl(PR_SVE_GET_VL) returns 512 before the crash. The kernel is 6.12 with ARM64_SVE enabled. It appears the thread's SVE context is saved with VL=512 and restored on an A520 core that only supports VL=256, leading to a stack corruption or vector register overflow. How should the kernel or the runtime handle asymmetric SVE vector lengths in a heterogeneous CSS cluster, and what scheduling constraints or prctl calls are required to prevent this migration hazard?
